svg.text: — Why the flow is built this way
One append-only log of Facts is the source of truth; every view, history tier, cascade, and live stream is a rebuildable projection of it.

g.text: Durable by construction
Every write is an fsync'd, sequenced entry in an
append-only commit log. A restart replays the log
and reconstructs the exact in-memory model —
nothing is ephemeral, nothing is lost.
Facts are exactly-once; increments never lose updates.
Two speeds, one truth
Facts commit synchronously and never drop — they
are structural truth. Observations are sampled
telemetry, queued and batched for throughput.
Both share one log and a unified property history.
High-volume telemetry never blocks the write path.
Snapshot + live, resumable
Clients subscribe once for a full snapshot of just
the objects they care about, then stream changes
over SSE. Drop the connection and resume gap-free
from any Last-Event-ID. No GET storm, no polling.
Language-agnostic — works for the polyglot fleet.
One log. Many lenses.
The Commit Log is the single source of truth. The live model, the time-series Rings, the state cascades, and the SSE feeds are all
projections of it — each independently rebuildable, none authoritative. Nothing is ephemeral. Nothing is lost. Everything can be replayed.
Which processes are hit? It depends on the input kind.
A Fact → VosModel (current value) · Rings (history, unless CurrentOnly) · Cascade via FactCommitReactor · live SSE model-change stream.
An Observation → VosModel · Canopy/Rings · Cascade via Hyphae. It does not hit the SSE model-change stream —
telemetry isn't pushed per-sample; clients read it from the history/current-value APIs instead.
Both publishers (ModelChangePublisher, FactCommitReactor) subscribe to FactsCommitted only — that is the design, not an omission.
🚧 Remaining work
Phase D — bulk Sediment loader (§6.13)
Massive historical loads written straight to sealed
Sapwood buckets. Deferred — streaming hybrid covers ingest.
Heartwood — cold archive tier (§7)
Age sealed Sapwood buckets out to cold storage.
